papers.title: Real-world evaluation of 2023–2024 XBB.1.5 mRNA and protein-based COVID-19 vaccine reactogenicity from the randomized BEEHIVE trial
papers.abstract: The objective of this analysis was to assess reactogenicity profile differences between a protein- and mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine in participants who had previously received ≥2 doses of an mRNA-based vaccine in a real-world, double-blinded, randomized, controlled trial. In the BEEHIVE/NCT06065176 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06065176), participants randomized 1:1 received one dose of the Novavax (NVX) or Pfizer–BioNTech (PFZ) COVID-19 vaccine 2023–2024 formulation (XBB.1.5); a comparator group did not receive a dose. Electronic surveys collected solicited systemic (fatigue, fever, headache, joint pain, malaise/feeling sick, muscle pain, and nausea/vomiting) and local (injection-site pain, tenderness, and swelling) events on days 1, 2, and 6 after study vaccination. Significantly lower proportions of participants in the NVX (n = 448) vs. PFZ (n = 453) group reported a systemic (62.1% vs. 75.7%; risk difference −13.7%, 95% CI: −19.6% to −7.7%) or local (81.0% vs. 92.7%; risk difference −11.7%, 95% CI: −16.0% to −7.3%) event in the day-1 survey (both Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel P 80% and >94% of participants in either group reported no systemic or local reactogenicity, respectively, in the day-6 survey. Mean number of events/person were significantly lower for the NVX vs. PFZ group in the day-1 (systemic and local) and day-2 (local) surveys (each P < .0001). There were significant differences in reactogenicity profiles for the 2023–2024 formulations of the NVX and PFZ COVID-19 vaccines, with NVX consistently associated with lower reactogenicity rates than PFZ.

papers.title: Safety Monitoring of COVID-19 Vaccines in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS): United States, August 22, 2024–July 4, 2025
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2024-2025 formulation for all Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccines licensed or authorized in the United States (US) was updated to a monovalent vaccine based on the Omicron JN.1 lineage of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Post-authorization and post-approval safety monitoring is important to ensure ongoing vaccine safety. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate and summarize reports to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) among persons who received the 2024-2025 formulation of the COVID-19 vaccines in the US. METHODS: We searched VAERS for US reports of individuals who received a COVID-19 vaccination and submitted a report during August 22, 2024, through July 4, 2025. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) clinicians reviewed reports and available medical records for selected adverse events of special interest (AESIs) and serious reports. For reports of death, the reported cause of death was based on the International Classification of Disease, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnostic categories reported on U.S. For reports of anaphylaxis and Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS), the Brighton Collaboration case definitions were used. For myocarditis, CDC's case definition was used. Reporting rates for the AESIs, excluding death, were estimated using vaccination coverage data for the 2024-2025 respiratory season. RESULTS: VAERS received 9856 reports after 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccination; 877 were serious (8.9%). The most common reported adverse events (AEs) included fever (854, 8.7%), pain (810, 8.2%), fatigue (785, 8.0%), headache (729, 7.4%), and dizziness (689, 7.0%). Of 273 deaths, cause of death was available for 97 reports, and the most common causes were diseases of the circulatory system (37, 38.1%), followed by diseases of the respiratory system (15, 15.5%). During the review period, no reports met the case definition of anaphylaxis, while eight reports met the Brighton case definition for GBS, and six reports met the case definition for myocarditis or myopericarditis. Death was not reported among the six myopericarditis cases. Reporting rates for GBS and myopericarditis were below background rates for these conditions. CONCLUSION: This review of AEs reported after the 2024-2025 formulation of the COVID-19 vaccines is consistent with previous observations after COVID-19 vaccination. Most reports were non-serious, and the most common AEs were consistent with known reactogenicity profiles. Ongoing safety monitoring of COVID-19 vaccines continues. Any potential risks of vaccine-related AEs should be considered in the context of the benefits of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing COVID-19 and its potentially serious complications.

papers.title: Wastewater-based genomic surveillance uncovers broader SARS-CoV-2 diversity and spatial transmission dynamics in Georgia, January 2023–July 2024
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater surveillance of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) using next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables real-time monitoring of circulating and emerging variants, often providing earlier detection than clinical reporting while capturing presymptomatic, asymptomatic, and symptomatic infections. However, the correlation between lineage abundance in wastewater and clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds in Georgia remains understudied. From January 2023 through July 2024, the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) sequenced SARS-CoV-2 from 669 wastewater samples collected across 17 treatment facilities in 15 counties. These data were compared with 325 clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds to assess early detection potential. Nucleic acids were extracted using the KingFisher Apex platform, followed by genomic library preparation and paired-end whole-genome sequencing on the Illumina NextSeq 2000. Variant calling and lineage abundance estimation using Freyja identified 2,218 SARS-CoV-2 lineages and sub-lineages, 1,769 in 2023, and 1,255 in 2024, with 806 co-circulating across both years. Clinical sequences spanned 135 lineages/sub-lineages across 15 clades, with >70% in clades 24A (27.4%), 23A (19.4%), 23F (13.5%), and 22E (10.2%). Predominant lineages included XBB.1.5 (11.4%), JN.1 (6.8%), and JN.1.4 (6.2%), reflecting broader clinical trends in Georgia. Clinical data also reflected distinct transmission patterns, including viral introduction and spread within and between counties. Overall, this study provides important insights into the introduction and dissemination of SARS-CoV-2 lineages in Georgia. Expanding wastewater surveillance to include other emerging and reemerging pathogens of public health importance will be particularly valuable during periods of low disease incidence, serving as an early warning system when clinical testing is limited and enabling timely public health responses. IMPORTANCE Wastewater-based surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 provides a noninvasive, cost-effective, population-level method for detecting viral genetic material independent of clinical testing. Next-generation sequencing enables timely monitoring of circulating lineages by public health laboratories. The Georgia National Wastewater Surveillance System (GA-NWSS) established in 2021 through collaboration between the Georgia Department of Public Health (DPH) Epidemiology and the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) collects weekly samples from 17 wastewater treatment facilities across 15 counties. From January 2023 through July 2024, GPHL sequenced 669 wastewater samples, identifying 2,218 SARS-CoV-2 lineages and sub-lineages, compared with 135 lineages detected in 325 clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds. Spatial analysis highlights viral spread across state boundaries and within Georgia catchment areas, illustrating evolving transmission patterns. These results demonstrate that wastewater sequencing captures broader genomic diversity than clinical sampling alone, emphasizing its critical role in pathogen genomic surveillance and supporting data-driven public health response to SARS-CoV-2.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 使用下一代测序(NGS)对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)进行污水监测,能够实现对循环和新兴变异株的实时监测,通常比临床报告更早发现,同时捕捉无症状、无症状和有症状感染。然而,佐治亚州对应排水系统中污水样本与临床样本的谱系丰度之间的相关性仍缺乏充分研究。从2023年1月至2024年7月,佐治亚公共卫生实验室(GPHL)从佐治亚州15个县的17个治疗设施中收集了669份污水样本,并对其进行了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2测序。这些数据与来自对应排水系统的325份临床样本进行了比较,以评估早期检测潜力。使用KingFisher Apex平台提取核酸,随后在Illumina NextSeq 2000上进行基因组文库制备和配对末端全基因组测序。使用Freyja进行变异检测和谱系丰度估计,共识别出2,218个严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系和亚谱系,其中2023年为1,769个,2024年为1,255个,有806个在两年间同时存在。临床序列覆盖了15个簇中的135个谱系/亚谱系,其中>70%属于24A(27.4%)、23A(19.4%)、23F(13.5%)和22E(10.2%)簇。主要谱系包括XBB.1.5(11.4%)、JN.1(6.8%)和JN.1.4(6.2%),反映了佐治亚州更广泛的临床趋势。临床数据还反映了独特的传播模式,包括病毒在县内及县间的引入和传播。总体而言,本研究为了解佐治亚州严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系的引入和传播提供了重要见解。在疾病发病率较低的时期,将污水监测扩展至包括其他对公共卫生重要的新兴和再出现病原体,将特别有价值,可以作为临床检测有限时的早期预警系统,并支持及时的公共卫生响应。重要性 基于污水的监测为检测病毒遗传物质提供了一种非侵入性、成本效益高且适用于人群水平的方法,独立于临床检测。下一代测序使公共卫生实验室能够及时监测循环谱系。2021年通过佐治亚公共卫生部门(DPH)与佐治亚公共卫生实验室(GPHL)的合作,建立了佐治亚国家污水监测系统(GA-NWSS),该系统每周从佐治亚州15个县的17个治疗设施中收集样本。从2023年1月至2024年7月,GPHL对669份污水样本进行了测序,识别出2,218个严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系和亚谱系,相比之下,来自对应排水系统的325份临床样本仅检测到135个谱系。空间分析突显了病毒在州边界和佐治亚州流域内的传播,展示了不断演变的传播模式。这些结果表明,污水测序能够捕捉比单独临床采样更广泛的基因组多样性,强调了其在病原体基因组监测中的关键作用,并支持对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的数据驱动型公共卫生响应。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 基于污水的基因组监测被需要以监测严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的多样性及空间传播动态,因为其能够比临床报告更早检测到新兴变异株。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究从2023年1月至2024年7月进行,涉及从佐治亚州15个县的17个治疗设施中收集的669份污水样本,以及来自相同排水系统的对应临床样本。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用KingFisher Apex平台提取核酸,随后在Illumina NextSeq 2000上进行基因组文库制备和配对末端全基因组测序。使用Freyja进行变异检测和谱系丰度估计。
analysis_zh.main_results: 污水测序识别出2,218个严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系和亚谱系,相比之下,来自对应排水系统的325份临床样本仅检测到135个谱系。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,污水测序能够捕捉比单独临床采样更广泛的基因组多样性,突显了其在病原体基因组监测中的关键作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为了解佐治亚州严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系的引入和传播提供了见解,支持对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的数据驱动型公共卫生响应。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它依赖于来自对应排水系统的污水样本和临床样本,可能在捕捉完整的临床图景方面存在局限性。

papers.title: Beyond correlation and causation: epistemic caution, anomalous findings, and COVID-19 vaccine safety
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed science's adaptive strengths and epistemic limits. In fact, in the pandemic, mRNA vaccines are attributed to have saved millions of lives. The maxim "correlation does not imply causation" is an essential safeguard against premature causal inference. However, its use may become epistemically restrictive when the absence of established causality is treated as sufficient reason not to investigate (severe) vaccine adverse events. This article examines the conditions under which a valid cautionary principle may have contributed to premature epistemic closure. Thomas Kuhn's theory of scientific paradigms is used as one interpretative lens rather than as an empirical explanation of institutional behaviour. We argue that the correlation-causation distinction can shift from a heuristic of caution to an instrument of epistemic conservatism, reinforcing prevailing frameworks and discouraging exploration of anomalies. A published autopsy case report involving multifocal necrotizing encephalitis and myocarditis after BNT162b2 vaccination is examined as an illustrative and hypothesis-generating case, not as representative evidence of systematic institutional conduct. A qualitative approach using Bradford Hill's criteria provides partial, inconclusive evidence of a causal relationship while also exposing the methodological limits of the tool employed. The results of the analysis showed that one of the nine criteria demonstrated support of causality, seven were partially supported, and one did not support causality. The analysis suggests, but does not prove, a causal relationship between the BNT162b2 vaccine and multifocal necrotizing encephalitis. The absence of the nucleocapsid protein does not provide definitive evidence to demonstrate a vaccine origin. Analytical methods are described which can distinguish between the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and the recombinant spike protein expressed following mRNA vaccination. The absence of evidence does not mean evidence of absence and we must keep an open mind to this when reviewing such evidence on causality.
papers.journal: Philosophy Ethics and Humanities in Medicine

analysis.scope_and_question: The article explores the epistemic caution and potential premature closure in assessing the safety of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, particularly focusing on the distinction between correlation and causation. It examines the conditions under which this cautionary principle may have influenced the investigation of vaccine adverse events, with a specific focus on the BNT162b2 vaccine and its association with multifocal necrotizing encephalitis and myocarditis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a qualitative analysis using Bradford Hill's criteria to assess the causal relationship between the BNT162b2 vaccine and multifocal necrotizing encephalitis. It includes a published autopsy case report as an illustrative and hypothesis-generating example, not as representative evidence of systematic institutional behavior. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates, but rather on the interpretation of a single case report.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The analysis suggests, but does not prove, a causal relationship between the BNT162b2 vaccine and multifocal necrotizing encephalitis. It highlights that the correlation-causation distinction can shift from a heuristic of caution to an instrument of epistemic conservatism, reinforcing existing frameworks and discouraging exploration of anomalies. The absence of the nucleocapsid protein does not provide definitive evidence to demonstrate a vaccine origin.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The article notes that the absence of evidence does not mean evidence of absence, emphasizing the need to maintain an open mind when reviewing causality. It also highlights the methodological limitations of Bradford Hill's criteria, which provide partial and inconclusive evidence of a causal relationship. The use of the correlation-causation distinction may become epistemically restrictive, preventing further investigation into severe vaccine adverse events.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The article describes analytical methods that can distinguish between the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and the recombinant spike protein expressed following mRNA vaccination. It calls for a more nuanced approach to evaluating vaccine safety, particularly in the context of severe adverse events, and suggests the need for further research and surveillance to address the evidence gaps and controversies surrounding vaccine causality.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the epistemic caution and potential premature closure in assessing the safety of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, particularly the BNT162b2 vaccine. It explores how the distinction between correlation and causation can shift from a heuristic to an instrument of epistemic conservatism, potentially discouraging the investigation of severe adverse events. The article uses a qualitative analysis of a published autopsy case report involving multifocal necrotizing encephalitis and myocarditis, highlighting the methodological limitations of Bradford Hill's criteria. It suggests that the absence of evidence does not equate to evidence of absence and calls for more nuanced analytical methods to distinguish between wild-type and recombinant spike proteins. The review emphasizes the need for further research and surveillance to address the evidence gaps and controversies surrounding vaccine causality.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述采用布拉德福德-希尔标准的定性分析方法,评估BNT162b2 疫苗与多灶性坏死性脑炎之间的因果关系。它包括一项已发表的尸检病例报告作为说明性和假设生成的例子,而非系统性机构行为的代表性证据。该综述未报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是对单一病例报告的解释进行分析。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分析表明,但并未证明BNT162b2 疫苗与多灶性坏死性脑炎之间存在因果关系。它指出,相关与因果的区分可能从一种谨慎的启发式方法转变为一种认识论保守主义的工具,强化现有框架并抑制对异常现象的探索。缺乏核衣壳蛋白并不能提供确定的证据来证明疫苗的起源。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本文指出,缺乏证据并不等于证据的缺失,强调在审查因果关系时必须保持开放心态。它还强调了布拉德福德-希尔标准的方法论局限,这些标准提供了因果关系的部分且不明确的证据。相关与因果的区分的使用可能变得认识论上具有限制性,阻碍对严重疫苗不良事件的进一步调查。

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 neutralising antibody profiles reveal variant specific antibody dynamics and regional differences in infection histories in Malawi
papers.abstract: Serological data provide important insights into SARS-CoV-2 transmission and immunity, particularly in regions with limited routine surveillance such as sub-Saharan Africa. However, antibody waning and boosting following reinfection or vaccination remain poorly characterised, complicating interpretation of serological measurements. Improved understanding of these dynamics is critical for accurate epidemiological inference. Modelling longitudinal serological data provides a means to quantify antibody kinetics and reconstruct infection histories. We analysed 15,679 neutralising antibody (nAb) titres from 1,675 unvaccinated, HIV-uninfected participants in urban (Lilongwe) and rural (Karonga) Malawi (February 2021-April 2022). NAb titres against ancestral B.1, Beta, Delta, and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) viruses were measured using an HIV-based SARS-CoV-2 pseudotyped virus neutralisation assay. A multi-level Bayesian model was used to reconstruct infection histories and antibody kinetics. The model identified 429 infections (95% credible interval 417-441), including 39 (9.1%) that had not been identified by traditional seroconversion-based thresholds. Antibody levels waned rapidly, with 48% (0.403-0.560) of the acute boost remaining after three months and only 5% (0.027-0.098) after one year. Pre-Omicron infections generated stronger antibody boosts than Omicron infections. Responses varied, with individuals clustering into low and high responders. Cross-reactive responses extended across substantial antigenic distances - Omicron infections induced broader immunity. Seroincidence was higher in Lilongwe than in Karonga (0.41 vs. 0.27 infections per person per three months), driven by the early 2022 Omicron wave. Reinfections were common, particularly among adults and urban residents. SARS-CoV-2 nAb responses following infection were heterogeneous and declined rapidly. This rapid waning underscores the importance of vaccination for sustained protection, while cross-reactivity suggests only partial immunity from prior variants. Identifying reinfections is essential for understanding transmission and finding populations at higher repeat infection risk, particularly where routine surveillance is limited.

A multi-level Bayesian model was used to reconstruct infection histories and antibody kinetics. The model identified 429 infections (95% credible interval 417-441), including 39 (9.1%) that had not been identified by traditional seroconversion-based thresholds. Antibody levels waned rapidly, with 48% (0.403-0.560) of the acute boost remaining after three months and only 5% (0.027-0.098) after one year. Pre-Omicron infections generated stronger antibody boosts than Omicron infections. Responses varied, with individuals clustering into low and high responders. Cross-reactive responses extended across substantial antigenic distances - Omicron infections induced broader immunity. Seroincidence was higher in Lilongwe than in Karonga (0.41 vs. 0.27 infections per person per three months), driven by the early 2022 Omicron wave. This rapid waning underscores the importance of vaccination for sustained protection, while cross-reactivity suggests only partial immunity from prior variants. Identifying reinfections is essential for understanding transmission and finding populations at higher repeat infection risk, particularly where routine surveillance is limited.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 中和抗体谱及其在马拉维的动态,以满足在疫苗接种率较低地区(尤其是撒哈拉以南非洲)对血清学数据的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在马拉维的城镇(利隆圭)和农村(卡龙加)地区进行,涉及 1,675 名未接种疫苗且未感染 HIV 的参与者,时间为 2021 年 2 月至 2022 年 4 月。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基于 HIV 的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 假型病毒中和试验测量了针对祖先 B.1、贝塔、德尔塔和奥密克戎(BA.1/BA.2)病毒的中和抗体滴度,并采用多水平贝叶斯模型来重建感染史和抗体动力学。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究识别出 429 次感染,发现抗体水平迅速下降,并且发现奥密克戎感染前的感染产生了更强的抗体增强反应。交叉反应性反应覆盖了相当大的抗原距离,奥密克戎感染诱导了更广泛的免疫力。利隆圭的血清学发病率高于卡龙加(每三人三个月内 0.41 与 0.27 次感染),这主要由 2022 年初的奥密克戎波峰所驱动。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明抗体迅速下降,且先前变种只能提供部分免疫力,突显了 疫苗接种 对持续保护的重要性,并强调了识别再感染对于理解 传播 和发现重复感染风险较高的群体的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的免疫情况提供了重要见解,特别是在撒哈拉以南非洲地区,并强调了准确流行病学推断和针对性公共卫生干预的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于缺乏对照组,以及样本人群可能存在偏倚,但其证据对于理解抗体动力学和感染史的地区差异具有较强的说服力。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的免疫情况提供了重要见解,特别是在撒哈拉以南非洲地区,并强调了准确流行病学推断和针对性公共卫生干预的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于缺乏对照组,以及样本人群可能存在偏倚,但其证据对于理解抗体动力学和感染史的地区差异具有较强的说服力。

papers.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir (Paxlovid) Versus Remdesivir in COVID‐19: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Retrospective Studies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aim Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) and remdesivir are antiviral agents that have been widely used in the management of patients with Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19). This systematic review and meta‐analysis were conducted to compare the clinical effectiveness and safety outcomes of Paxlovid and remdesivir among patients with COVID‐19. Methods A systematic search was performed across the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, PubMed, and medRxiv from inception to July 2024. Data from the identified studies were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta‐Analysis (CMA) software. Results Thirteen studies involving 4583 patients were included in the final analysis. Compared with remdesivir, Paxlovid was associated with a significant reduction in mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 0.36, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.18–0.73), time to SARS‐CoV‐2 negative conversion (standardized mean differences [SMD] = −1.44, 95% CI: −1.54 to −1.33), hospitalization (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.16–0.74), intensive care unit admission (OR = 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01–0.53), and the need for oxygen therapy (OR = 0.06, 95% CI: 0.02–0.16). No statistically significant difference was observed between the two treatments regarding polymerase chain reaction negativity rate (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 0.73–2.86). However, adverse events were higher among patients receiving Paxlovid (OR = 6.60, 95% CI: 3.24–13.42). The certainty of evidence for the evaluated outcomes ranged from low to moderate. Conclusion In patients with COVID‐19, Paxlovid may offer potential benefits over remdesivir for certain clinical outcomes, though it may also be accompanied by a higher rate of adverse events. These findings are based on retrospective studies, which carry risks of selection bias, confounding, and heterogeneity.

Data from the identified studies were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta‐Analysis (CMA) software. Results Thirteen studies involving 4583 patients were included in the final analysis. Compared with remdesivir, Paxlovid was associated with a significant reduction in mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 0.36, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.18–0.73), time to SARS‐CoV‐2 negative conversion (standardized mean differences [SMD] = −1.44, 95% CI: −1.54 to −1.33), hospitalization (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.16–0.74), intensive care unit admission (OR = 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01–0.53), and the need for oxygen therapy (OR = 0.06, 95% CI: 0.02–0.16). No statistically significant difference was observed between the two treatments regarding polymerase chain reaction negativity rate (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 0.73–2.86). However, adverse events were higher among patients receiving Paxlovid (OR = 6.60, 95% CI: 3.24–13.42). The certainty of evidence for the evaluated outcomes ranged from low to moderate. Conclusion In patients with COVID‐19, Paxlovid may offer potential benefits over remdesivir for certain clinical outcomes, though it may also be accompanied by a higher rate of adverse events. These findings are based on retrospective studies, which carry risks of selection bias, confounding, and heterogeneity.

papers.title: The Value of Time-to-Onset for Signal Validation: Experience from the Reporting of COVID-19 Vaccines and Glomerular Diseases in VigiBase.
papers.abstract: Background Adverse event reports of glomerular diseases (GDs) following coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination collected nationally have been shared to VigiBase, the global database of adverse event reports for medicines and vaccines. From literature reports, different GDs following COVID-19 vaccination have different time-to-onsets (TTOs), highlighting the potential value of TTO in suggesting underlying disease mechanisms and supporting its relevance in signal validation prior to in-depth signal assessment. Objective The aim of this study was to characterise the TTO in reports of GDs in association with COVID-19 vaccines inVigiBase. The analysis focuses on exploring the value of TTO for signal validation, an early step preceding signal assessment. analysis.summary_en: This review explores the value of time-to-onset (TTO) in signal validation for adverse events following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. The study analysed 245 unique cases of glomerular diseases (GDs) reported in VigiBase, focusing on differences in TTO between GDs and within GDs by disease status. The findings suggest that TTO data may provide additional insights into disease mechanisms and complement traditional disproportionality analysis. However, the study also highlights the need for further research to validate these hypotheses and improve signal validation methods for SARS-CoV-2 vaccines.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括2023年4月3日从VigiBase中提取的四种不同肾小球疾病与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗相关的报告。报告进行了去重处理,并手动验证了时间至发病信息。按肾小球疾病类型总结了人口学和临床特征,并在每种疾病中比较了不同疾病状态(复发和新发病例)的中位时间至发病。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本研究在VigiBase中识别出245个与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗相关的肾小球疾病独特病例。大多数病例涉及messenger RNA 疫苗,且大多数发生在第二剂之后。观察到肾小球疾病之间以及每种疾病内部不同疾病状态之间的中位时间至发病差异,但只有IgA肾小球肾炎与其他三种肾小球疾病之间的差异具有统计学意义。本研究突显了时间至发病在与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗相关的不良事件信号验证中的潜在价值。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究指出,肾小球疾病之间以及每种疾病内部不同疾病状态之间的中位时间至发病差异并不一致具有统计学意义,除了IgA肾小球肾炎与其他三种肾小球疾病之间的差异。这表明,尽管时间至发病可能提供一些见解,但其在信号验证中的作用仍有限,需要进一步研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本研究表明,时间至发病数据可以在与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗相关的不良事件信号验证的早期阶段补充传统比例分析。它还强调了需要进一步研究时间至发病差异是否可能表明潜在的疾病机制。

papers.title: Payers should cover COVID-19 vaccines for all ages and risk groups with no patient cost sharing.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 vaccine saved millions of lives during the pandemic. Clinical trials at the time of authorization and approval showed remarkable effectiveness. However, the effectiveness of the COVID-19 vaccine has changed now that people are no longer naive to the virus. The benefit of vaccination is incrementally lower for some people, raising questions about who should receive the vaccine, what the vaccines should cost, and which subpopulations would be cost-effective to vaccinate. The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review (ICER) recently released its assessment of the COVID-19 vaccine. It was ICER's first vaccine assessment, presumably because of the uncertainty of future coverage policies for the COVID-19 vaccine. ICER found that the COVID-19 vaccine is most beneficial for the very young, the very old, and those in between with risk factors. Cost-effectiveness models mirror effectiveness assessments. Limiting vaccine access to people with risk factors in specific age bands would require a prior authorization, adding complexity and administrative costs for payers. Coverage restrictions may further reduce population vaccinations rates, resulting in higher virus community load and prolonged circulation. Although the US regulatory framework requires insurers to cover vaccines included on the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Immunization Schedules without cost sharing, the future placement of COVID-19 vaccines on these schedules is uncertain. Given the evidence and population benefits, we support ICER's recommendation for private payers to cover COVID-19 vaccines with no patient cost sharing. We further recommend no restrictions on coverage based on risk factors, regardless of CDC Immunization Schedules, which have recently been subject to considerable uncertainty.
papers.journal: Journal of Managed Care & Specialty Pharmacy

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the coverage of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, specifically addressing whether payers should cover them for all ages and risk groups without patient cost sharing. The central question is about the equitable and cost-effective distribution of vaccines, with the pandemic context and the evolving effectiveness of vaccines over time as key considerations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on clinical trial data from the time of vaccine authorization and approval, which demonstrated remarkable effectiveness. It also references the Institute for Clinical and Economic Review (ICER) assessment of the vaccine, which is noted as its first vaccine evaluation due to the uncertainty surrounding future coverage policies. The US regulatory framework is mentioned, requiring insurers to cover vaccines on the CDC Immunization Schedules without cost sharing, though the future placement of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine on these schedules is uncertain.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine is most beneficial for the very young, the very old, and those with risk factors. It also states that cost-effectiveness models align with effectiveness assessments, supporting the recommendation for private payers to cover the vaccine without cost sharing. The review further emphasizes that coverage restrictions based on risk factors may reduce vaccination rates and lead to prolonged virus circulation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the effectiveness of the vaccine has changed as people are no longer naive to the virus, raising questions about its incremental benefit for certain subpopulations. It also highlights the uncertainty surrounding the future placement of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine on the CDC Immunization Schedules, which affects coverage policies. Additionally, the review suggests that limiting access to specific age bands or risk groups may introduce administrative complexity and reduce vaccination rates.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends that private payers should cover the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine with no patient cost sharing, regardless of CDC Immunization Schedules. It also advocates for no restrictions on coverage based on risk factors, emphasizing the need for equitable access to ensure high vaccination rates and reduce community virus load.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the cost-effectiveness and equity of covering SARS-CoV-2 vaccines for all ages and risk groups without patient cost sharing. It highlights the remarkable effectiveness of vaccines as demonstrated in clinical trials and notes that their benefit has diminished as population immunity has increased. The review supports the Institute for Clinical and Economic Review (ICER) recommendation for universal coverage, citing the importance of equitable access in maintaining high vaccination rates and reducing virus circulation. It also emphasizes the need for payers to avoid restrictions based on risk factors, as these may complicate administration and reduce overall vaccine uptake.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本审查聚焦于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗的覆盖问题,具体探讨支付方是否应为所有年龄段和风险群体覆盖该疫苗,无需患者自付费用。核心问题是关于疫苗的公平且成本效益的分配,以疫情期间的背景以及该疫苗随时间推移的效果变化为关键考虑因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述基于疫苗授权和批准时的临床试验数据,这些数据展示了显著的有效性。它还参考了临床与经济审查研究所(ICER)对疫苗的评估,由于未来覆盖政策的不确定性,该评估被特别指出是其首次疫苗评估。文中提到了美国的监管框架,要求保险公司根据CDC免疫接种计划覆盖疫苗且不涉及费用分摊,尽管严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗在未来这些计划中的位置仍存在不确定性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本审查得出结论,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗对非常年幼、非常年长以及具有风险因素的中间年龄段人群最为有益。它还指出,成本效益模型与效果评估一致,支持私人支付方无需患者自付费用即可覆盖疫苗的建议。本审查进一步强调,基于风险因素的覆盖限制可能会降低人群疫苗接种率,并导致病毒传播周期延长。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本审查指出,随着人们对病毒不再天真,疫苗的效果已发生变化,这引发了关于其对某些亚人群的增量效益的问题。它还强调了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗未来是否会被列入CDC免疫计划的不确定性,这影响了覆盖政策。此外,本审查建议将疫苗的覆盖限制在特定年龄组或风险群体可能会引入行政复杂性并降低疫苗接种率。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本审查建议私人支付方应无需患者自付费用即可覆盖严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗,无论CDC免疫计划如何变化。它还倡导不应基于风险因素对覆盖进行限制,强调确保公平获取以维持高疫苗接种率并减少社区病毒负荷的必要性。}}.{

papers.title: Cardiovascular and mortality risks following COVID-19-related versus non-COVID-19-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations.
papers.abstract: RATIONALE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations, often triggered by viral infections like COVID-19, are associated with increased cardiovascular risk. We hypothesized that COVID-19-related exacerbations carry higher short-term cardiovascular and mortality risks than non-COVID-19-related exacerbations. OBJECTIVES: To compare 28-day risk of stroke, pulmonary embolism (PE), acute myocardial infarction (AMI), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality following COVID-19-related vs non-COVID-19-related COPD exacerbations and assess variation across the pandemic. METHODS: Using Swedish national registers, we identified COPD with moderate (treated with oral corticosteroids with/without antibiotics) or severe (hospitalized) exacerbations from March 2020 to June 2023. Exacerbations with infection, hospitalization, or intensive care admission for COVID-19 were defined as COVID-19 related. A target trial was emulated and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated for each outcome, stratified by exacerbation severity and COVID-19 variants. RESULTS: Among 266 273 exacerbations (87.2% moderate, 12.8% severe), 5425 (2%) were COVID-19 related. COVID-19-related vs non-COVID-19-related moderate exacerbations were associated with risk of PE (aHR, 2.26 [95% CI, 1.49-3.42]), overall cardiovascular events (1.94 [1.47-2.56]), MACE (1.88 [1.28-2.76]), and mortality (4.58 [4.06-5.17]), but not significantly with AMI and stroke. Severe COVID-19-related exacerbations were only associated with higher mortality (1.46 [1.28-1.66]). Cardiovascular risks were highest during pre-Alpha and Delta for moderate exacerbations. Mortality remained elevated for both moderate and severe exacerbations, particularly during the same periods. CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19-related exacerbations increased MACE, short-term cardiovascular, and mortality risks, mainly for moderate exacerbations, with attenuation during Alpha and Omicron, highlighting the need for proactive cardiovascular care during respiratory outbreaks.
papers.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cardiovascular and mortality risks associated with COPD exacerbations triggered by COVID-19 compared to those caused by other viruses. Using Swedish national registers, researchers identified COPD exacerbations from March 2020 to June 2023 and classified them as either related to or unrelated to COVID-19. They found that moderate exacerbations linked to COVID-19 had significantly higher risks of pulmonary embolism, cardiovascular events, major adverse cardiovascular events, and mortality compared to non-COVID-19-related exacerbations. However, these risks were less pronounced during the Alpha and Omicron variants. The study highlights the need for targeted cardiovascular monitoring in patients with COPD exacerbations during respiratory outbreaks. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and potential confounding factors.

papers.title_zh: Cardiovascular and mortality risks following COVID-19-related versus non-COVID-19-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations.
papers.source_body_en: RATIONALE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations, often triggered by viral infections like COVID-19, are associated with increased cardiovascular risk. We hypothesized that COVID-19-related exacerbations carry higher short-term cardiovascular and mortality risks than non-COVID-19-related exacerbations. OBJECTIVES: To compare 28-day risk of stroke, pulmonary embolism (PE), acute myocardial infarction (AMI), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality following COVID-19-related vs non-COVID-19-related COPD exacerbations and assess variation across the pandemic. METHODS: Using Swedish national registers, we identified COPD with moderate (treated with oral corticosteroids with/without antibiotics) or severe (hospitalized) exacerbations from March 2020 to June 2023. Exacerbations with infection, hospitalization, or intensive care admission for COVID-19 were defined as COVID-19 related. A target trial was emulated and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated for each outcome, stratified by exacerbation severity and COVID-19 variants. RESULTS: Among 266 273 exacerbations (87.2% moderate, 12.8% severe), 5425 (2%) were COVID-19 related. COVID-19-related vs non-COVID-19-related moderate exacerbations were associated with risk of PE (aHR, 2.26 [95% CI, 1.49-3.42]), overall cardiovascular events (1.94 [1.47-2.56]), MACE (1.88 [1.28-2.76]), and mortality (4.58 [4.06-5.17]), but not significantly with AMI and stroke. Severe COVID-19-related exacerbations were only associated with higher mortality (1.46 [1.28-1.66]). Cardiovascular risks were highest during pre-Alpha and Delta for moderate exacerbations. Mortality remained elevated for both moderate and severe exacerbations, particularly during the same periods. CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19-related exacerbations increased MACE, short-term cardiovascular, and mortality risks, mainly for moderate exacerbations, with attenuation during Alpha and Omicron, highlighting the need for proactive cardiovascular care during respiratory outbreaks.

papers.title: Raman Analysis of RNA Nucleotide Strands From SARS‐CoV‐2 Variants and Subvariants: A Step Forward in the Definition of “Raman Genome”
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Raman spectra of RNA nucleotide strands extracted from 20 SARS‐CoV‐2 strains, including the original Japanese isolate, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Lambda, Theta, Mu, and 12 Omicron subvariants, were systematically collected, deconvoluted, and converted into Raman barcodes. The spectra exhibited common features associated with the RNA backbone, ribofuranose rings, and nitrogenous bases, reflecting the overall structural similarity of the viral RNAs. However, distinct differences were observed in spectral signatures related to β‐D‐ribofuranose vibrations, phosphate linkages, and RNA bases sensitive to secondary‐structure variations. Conventional principal component analysis provided only limited discrimination among variants and subvariants. In contrast, Raman barcodes captured subtle molecular‐scale structural differences and successfully distinguished all investigated strains according to their RNA secondary structures. The analysis identified vibrational markers associated with nucleotide chain length, backbone conformation, and ribofuranose dynamics. Several backbone‐ and base‐related signals exhibited hyperchromic behavior correlated with RNA secondary‐structure features, including hairpin content and stem length. These relationships may serve as indicators for the rapid detection of emerging variants. By encoding key spectral signatures, Raman barcodes provide a robust framework for accurate classification of SARS‐CoV‐2 strains based on the molecular architecture of their RNAs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the potential of Raman spectroscopy for distinguishing SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants through their RNA structural features, addressing the need for rapid and accurate detection methods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved systematic collection and analysis of Raman spectra from RNA nucleotide strands of 20 SARS-CoV-2 strains, including the original Japanese isolate and various variants and subvariants such as Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Lambda, Theta, Mu, and 12 Omicron subvariants.
analysis.methods: Raman spectra were collected, deconvoluted, and converted into Raman barcodes to capture molecular-scale structural differences. Principal component analysis was used to assess the discrimination capabilities among variants and subvariants.
analysis.main_results: Conventional principal component analysis provided limited discrimination, while Raman barcodes successfully distinguished all investigated strains based on their RNA secondary structures. The analysis identified vibrational markers linked to nucleotide chain length, backbone conformation, and ribofuranose dynamics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Raman barcodes can effectively encode key spectral signatures for accurate classification of SARS-CoV-2 strains, offering a novel approach to molecular-level structural analysis of viral RNA.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform the development of rapid detection methods for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, enhancing surveillance and response capabilities during pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to spectral analysis without functional or clinical outcomes, and the evidence is based on a relatively small number of strains, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of Raman spectroscopy to distinguish SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants by analyzing their RNA structural features. Raman spectra of 20 strains, including the original Japanese isolate and various variants, were collected and converted into Raman barcodes. The analysis revealed that while conventional principal component analysis provided limited discrimination, Raman barcodes successfully differentiated all strains based on RNA secondary structures. The study identified vibrational markers associated with nucleotide chain length, backbone conformation, and ribofuranose dynamics, suggesting that Raman barcodes could offer a novel method for rapid detection of emerging variants. The findings may enhance surveillance and response efforts for SARS-CoV-2. However, the study is limited to spectral analysis without functional or clinical outcomes, and the evidence is based on a relatively small number of strains, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探索拉曼光谱在通过RNA结构特征区分严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株和亚变种方面的潜力,以应对快速且准确检测方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及系统收集和分析20种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2菌株(包括原始日本分离株以及各种变异株和亚变种,如Alpha、Beta、Gamma、Delta、Lambda、Theta、Mu和12种奥密克戎亚变种)的RNA核苷酸链的拉曼光谱。
elements_zh.methods: 拉曼光谱被收集、解卷积并转换为拉曼条形码,以捕捉分子级的结构差异。主成分分析被用于评估变异株和亚变种之间的区分能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 传统的主成分分析仅能提供有限的区分能力,而拉曼条形码能够根据RNA二级结构成功区分所有研究的菌株。分析确定了与核苷酸链长度、骨架构象和核糖呋喃环动力学相关的振动标记。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,拉曼条形码能够有效编码关键光谱特征,为严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2菌株的准确分类提供新方法,从而实现病毒RNA分子级结构分析的新途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于开发针对新出现严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株的快速检测方法,增强监测在大流行期间的监测和应对能力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于光谱分析,未涉及功能或临床结果,且证据基于相对较少的菌株,这可能影响其普遍适用性。证据强度为中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 从20种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2菌株(包括原始日本分离株、Alpha、Beta、Gamma、Delta、Lambda、Theta、Mu以及12种奥密克戎亚变种)中提取的RNA核苷酸链的拉曼光谱被系统地收集、解卷积并转换为拉曼条形码。光谱表现出与RNA骨架、核糖呋喃环和含氮碱基相关的共同特征,反映了病毒RNA的整体结构相似性。然而,在与β-D-核糖呋喃环振动、磷酸键和对二级结构变化敏感的RNA碱基相关的光谱特征中观察到了显著差异。传统的主成分分析仅能提供有限的变异株和亚变种区分能力。相比之下,拉曼条形码能够捕捉细微的分子级结构差异,并根据RNA二级结构成功区分了所有研究的菌株。分析确定了与核苷酸链长度、骨架构象和核糖呋喃环动力学相关的振动标记。一些与骨架和碱基相关的信号表现出与RNA二级结构特征(包括发夹结构含量和茎长度)相关的增色效应。这些关系可能作为快速检测新出现变异株的指标。通过编码关键光谱特征,拉曼条形码为基于其RNA分子结构的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2菌株准确分类提供了稳健的框架。

papers.title: Mpox Vaccine Acceptance Among Health Care Workers in Central Asia: The Role of COVID-19 Experience.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic may have shaped health care workers’ (HCWs’) perceptions of emerging infectious threats and willingness to adopt new vaccines. This study examined whether COVID-19-related experiences and psychological factors were associated with Mpox vaccine acceptance among HCWs in Central Asia. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 3,054 HCWs from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan completed an online survey between July and November 2022. Mpox vaccine acceptance was assessed using a single 5-point Likert-scale item and analyzed as a continuous outcome. Measures included COVID-19-related experiences, fear of COVID-19 and Mpox, DASS-21, and occupational burnout. Analyses included comparative tests, multivariable linear regression, and exploratory mediation models. Results Overall, 1,868 HCWs (61.2%) reported some willingness to receive Mpox vaccination, whereas 1,186 (38.8%) reported none. In bivariate analyses, acceptance varied by country and was higher among HCWs with COVID-19 frontline experience or living with high-risk individuals. In multivariable regression, fear of Mpox was the strongest correlate of acceptance, while burnout was inversely associated. Mediation analyses indicated indirect associations through fear- and distress-related pathways. Conclusions Mpox vaccine acceptance among Central Asian HCWs was associated with pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk. Strategies should combine risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support.
papers.journal: Disaster Medicine and Public Health Preparedness

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how the experiences of the COVID-19 pandemic influenced health care workers’ (HCWs’) willingness to accept the Mpox vaccine in Central Asia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 3,054 HCWs from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan between July and November 2022.
analysis.methods: Mpox vaccine acceptance was measured using a single 5-point Likert-scale item and analyzed as a continuous outcome. Statistical analyses included comparative tests, multivariable linear regression, and exploratory mediation models.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk were associated with Mpox vaccine acceptance among Central Asian HCWs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strategies should integrate risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support to improve Mpox vaccine acceptance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated Mpox vaccine acceptance among health care workers (HCWs) in Central Asia, focusing on the influence of their experiences with the COVID-19 pandemic and psychological factors. A cross-sectional survey of 3,054 HCWs from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan was conducted between July and November 2022. Mpox vaccine acceptance was assessed using a 5-point Likert scale and treated as a continuous outcome. The study found that 61.2% of HCWs expressed some willingness to receive the Mpox vaccine, while 38.8% did not. Fear of Mpox was strongly correlated with acceptance, whereas burnout was inversely associated. Mediation analyses suggested indirect effects through fear- and distress-related pathways. The authors concluded that pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk were linked to vaccine acceptance, highlighting the need for strategies that combine risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit its ability to establish causality.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how the experiences of the COVID-19 pandemic influenced health care workers’ (HCWs’) willingness to accept the Mpox vaccine in Central Asia.
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年 7 月至 11 月期间,在哈萨克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦的 3,054 名医护人员中开展了一项横断面研究。
elements_zh.methods: 通过单个 5 分 Likert 量表项目测量 Mpox 疫苗 接受度,并将其作为连续变量进行分析。统计分析包括比较检验、多变量线性回归和探索性中介模型。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,1,868 名医护人员(61.2%)表示愿意接受 Mpox 疫苗接种,而 1,186 名(38.8%)表示不愿意。在多变量回归分析中,对 Mpox 的恐惧是接受度最强的预测因素,而职业倦怠则呈负相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,大流行经历和对传染病风险的心理反应与中亚地区医护人员对 Mpox 疫苗 的接受度相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,应将风险沟通与职业倦怠减少及医护人员福祉支持相结合,以提高 Mpox 疫苗 的接受度。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于横断面设计,无法确定因果关系,且依赖自我报告数据,可能引入偏倚。

analysis_en.methods: Mpox vaccine acceptance was measured using a single 5-point Likert-scale item and analyzed as a continuous outcome. Statistical analyses included comparative tests, multivariable linear regression, and exploratory mediation models.
analysis_en.main_results: Overall, 1,868 HCWs (61.2%) reported some willingness to receive Mpox vaccination, whereas 1,186 (38.8%) reported none. In multivariable regression, fear of Mpox was the strongest correlate of acceptance, while burnout was inversely associated.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk were associated with Mpox vaccine acceptance among Central Asian HCWs.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strategies should integrate risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support to improve Mpox vaccine acceptance.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias.

papers.title_zh: Mpox Vaccine Acceptance Among Health Care Workers in Central Asia: The Role of COVID-19 Experience.
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic may have shaped health care workers’ (HCWs’) perceptions of emerging infectious threats and willingness to adopt new vaccines. This study examined whether COVID-19-related experiences and psychological factors were associated with Mpox vaccine acceptance among HCWs in Central Asia. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 3,054 HCWs from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan completed an online survey between July and November 2022. Mpox vaccine acceptance was assessed using a single 5-point Likert-scale item and analyzed as a continuous outcome. Measures included COVID-19-related experiences, fear of COVID-19 and Mpox, DASS-21, and occupational burnout. Analyses included comparative tests, multivariable linear regression, and exploratory mediation models. Results Overall, 1,868 HCWs (61.2%) reported some willingness to receive Mpox vaccination, whereas 1,186 (38.8%) reported none. In bivariate analyses, acceptance varied by country and was higher among HCWs with COVID-19 frontline experience or living with high-risk individuals. In multivariable regression, fear of Mpox was the strongest correlate of acceptance, while burnout was inversely associated. Mediation analyses indicated indirect associations through fear- and distress-related pathways. Conclusions Mpox vaccine acceptance among Central Asian HCWs was associated with pandemic experience and psychological responses to infectious disease risk. Strategies should combine risk communication with burnout reduction and HCW well-being support.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年 7 月至 11 月期间,在哈萨克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦的 3,054 名医护人员中开展了一项横断面研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过单个 5 分 Likert 量表项目测量 Mpox 疫苗 接受度,并将其作为连续变量进行分析。统计分析包括比较检验、多变量线性回归和探索性中介模型。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体而言,1,868 名医护人员(61.2%)表示愿意接受 Mpox 疫苗接种,而 1,186 名(38.8%)表示不愿意。在多变量回归分析中,对 Mpox 的恐惧是接受度最强的预测因素,而职业倦怠则呈负相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,大流行经历和对传染病风险的心理反应与中亚地区医护人员对 Mpox 疫苗 的接受度相关。

papers.title: Indirect effects of PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms on the association between COVID-19 cases/symptoms and intimate partner violence perpetration in the United States.
papers.abstract: Although rates of intimate partner violence (IPV) tend to rise following natural disasters, partly via trauma-related symptoms, the trauma-specific mechanisms underlying IPV perpetration during epidemics and pandemics such as COVID-19 remain unclear. Therefore, the aim of this study was to examine the association between COVID-19 (its incidence or symptoms) and IPV and the contribution of trauma-related symptoms to such association during the first wave of the pandemic (March-April 2020). This study applied generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling to analyze data from a demographically diverse U.S. online panel survey ( N = 1,183). The variables included self-reported data of IPV perpetration, posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety, and COVID-19 symptoms ("likely COVID-19"). Additionally, we examined COVID-19 state-level data for tested and confirmed cases as reported by the Johns Hopkins University Center during March 2020 ("tested COVID-19"). Groups in states with higher incidence of COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IPV perpetration than groups in states with lower incidence of COVID-19. Furthermore, the findings indicated that posttraumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms were indirectly associated with likely COVID-19 symptoms and psychological and physical IPV perpetration. These results suggested a connection between COVID-19 and IPV perpetration and indicated how trauma-related symptoms affected this association. The results underscore that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises such as pandemics are a risk factor for IPV perpetration. Trauma-informed screening and intervention can be useful in identifying and reducing IPV during the early stages of such crises. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title_original: Indirect effects of PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms on the association between COVID-19 cases/symptoms and intimate partner violence perpetration in the United States.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to examine the association between COVID-19 (its incidence or symptoms) and intimate partner violence (IPV) and to explore the indirect effects of trauma-related symptoms (posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety) on this association during the first wave of the pandemic (March-April 2020).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study used generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling to analyze data from an online panel survey (N = 1,183). The variables included self-reported data of IPV perpetration, posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety, and COVID-19 symptoms ("likely COVID-19"). State-level data on tested and confirmed cases of COVID-19 were also examined.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Groups in states with higher incidence of COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IPV perpetration than groups in states with lower incidence. The findings indicated that posttraumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms were indirectly associated with likely COVID-19 symptoms and psychological and physical IPV perpetration. These results suggested a connection between COVID-19 and IPV perpetration and indicated how trauma-related symptoms affected this association.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not report on the specific mechanisms linking trauma-related symptoms to IPV perpetration. It also did not address the potential role of anxiety symptoms in this association. The evidence does not clarify whether the observed associations were causal or merely correlational.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The results underscore that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises such as pandemics are a risk factor for IPV perpetration. Trauma-informed screening and intervention can be useful in identifying and reducing IPV during the early stages of such crises.

analysis.summary_en: This review article investigates the indirect effects of PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms on the association between COVID-19 cases/symptoms and intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration in the United States. The study analyzed data from an online panel survey (N = 1,183) using generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling. It found that states with higher COVID-19 incidence had higher rates of IPV perpetration, and that PTSD and depression symptoms were indirectly linked to likely COVID-19 symptoms and IPV. The findings suggest that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises may increase IPV risk. The study highlights the need for trauma-informed screening and interventions to address IPV in pandemic contexts. However, it does not explore the role of anxiety symptoms or clarify the causal mechanisms behind the observed associations.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The study aimed to examine the association between COVID-19 (its incidence or symptoms) and intimate partner violence (IPV) and to explore the indirect effects of trauma-related symptoms (posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety) on this association during the first wave of the pandemic (March-April 2020).
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study used generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling to analyze data from an online panel survey (N = 1,183). The variables included self-reported data of IPV perpetration, posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety, and COVID-19 symptoms ("likely COVID-19"). State-level data on tested and confirmed cases of COVID-19 were also examined.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Groups in states with higher incidence of COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IPV perpetration than groups in states with lower incidence. The findings indicated that posttraumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms were indirectly associated with likely COVID-19 symptoms and psychological and physical IPV perpetration. These results suggested a connection between COVID-19 and IPV perpetration and indicated how trauma-related symptoms affected this association.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not report on the specific mechanisms linking trauma-related symptoms to IPV perpetration. It also did not address the potential role of anxiety symptoms in this association. The evidence does not clarify whether the observed associations were causal or merely correlational.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The results underscore that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises such as pandemics are a risk factor for IPV perpetration. Trauma-informed screening and intervention can be useful in identifying and reducing IPV during the early stages of such crises.

papers.title_zh: Indirect effects of PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms on the association between COVID-19 cases/symptoms and intimate partner violence perpetration in the United States.
papers.source_body_en: Although rates of intimate partner violence (IPV) tend to rise following natural disasters, partly via trauma-related symptoms, the trauma-specific mechanisms underlying IPV perpetration during epidemics and pandemics such as COVID-19 remain unclear. Therefore, the aim of this study was to examine the association between COVID-19 (its incidence or symptoms) and IPV and the contribution of trauma-related symptoms to such association during the first wave of the pandemic (March-April 2020). This study applied generalized linear modeling and structural equation modeling to analyze data from a demographically diverse U.S. online panel survey ( N = 1,183). The variables included self-reported data of IPV perpetration, posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, anxiety, and COVID-19 symptoms ("likely COVID-19"). Additionally, we examined COVID-19 state-level data for tested and confirmed cases as reported by the Johns Hopkins University Center during March 2020 ("tested COVID-19"). Groups in states with higher incidence of COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IPV perpetration than groups in states with lower incidence of COVID-19. Furthermore, the findings indicated that posttraumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms were indirectly associated with likely COVID-19 symptoms and psychological and physical IPV perpetration. These results suggested a connection between COVID-19 and IPV perpetration and indicated how trauma-related symptoms affected this association. The results underscore that trauma-related symptoms during public health crises such as pandemics are a risk factor for IPV perpetration. Trauma-informed screening and intervention can be useful in identifying and reducing IPV during the early stages of such crises. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Sequential Combined Immunomodulatory Systemic Therapies Used in the Management of Refractory Cytokine Release Syndrome in Critically Ill Patients with COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Introduction/objective Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is characterized by systemic hyperinflammation and cytokine storm, a series of clinical conditions caused by excessive immune reactions. Although numerous studies have been conducted on anti-inflammatory treatments for severe COVID-19, no specific recommendations have been made regarding drugs to use in patients with Refractory Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) after the use of first-line anticytokine drugs. The objective of this report was to evaluate the efficacy of sequential immunomodulatory therapies in the management of refractory CRS in COVID-19 patients. Methods From March 2020 to March 2023, 1,025 patients with COVID-19 were admitted to the Infectious and Tropical Diseases ward at the Annunziata Cosenza Hub Hospital in Cosenza, Italy. To determine how many patients with refractory COVID-19-associated CRS were treated with combinedsequential therapy involving tocilizumab, a recombinant humanized anti-Interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor monoclonal antibody, and baricitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor, or anakinra, a recombinant human interleukin- 1 receptor antagonist, the electronic medical records of all hospitalized patients with COVID-19 were reviewed. The primary outcome was the incidence of CRS by day 29. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and 30-day mortality, to assess hospital performance and patient safety. Electronic databases such as MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Central were searched through June 30, 2026, for case-series and studies evaluating the efficacy of sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies in the management of refractory CRS in critically ill patients with COVID-19. Results From January 2021 to December 2023, a total of 25 patients received sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies, including tocilizumab and baricitinib or anakinra, in the management of COVID-19-related CRS. After 72 hours from the introduction of the new anti-cytokine therapy, a significant improvement of respiratory parameters, clinical state, inflammatory markers, and blood counts was observed. All patients survived, and those 5 previously mechanically ventilated patients were extubated. Non-infectious or infectious pulmonary or systemic complications were observed in all patients who underwent sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies. Discussion The study's findings suggest that tocilizumab used in sequential combination with baricitinib or anakinra, in conjunction with standard of care treatments, was associated with improved outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19 disease and early discharge from the hospital. Conclusion There is clear rationale for using combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies in critically ill patients who develop refractory CRS. The results of the experience, supported by a review of the current literature, suggest the need for larger-scale studies on sequential and combined systemic immunomodulatory therapies to manage refractory CRS in critically ill patients with COVID-19.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the efficacy and safety of sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies—tocilizumab paired with baricitinib or anakinra—for treating refractory cytokine release syndrome in critically ill patients with COVID‐19.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the use of sequential combined immunomodulatory therapies—tocilizumab with baricitinib or anakinra—in critically ill COVID‐19 patients suffering from refractory cytokine release syndrome. A retrospective analysis of 1,025 admissions identified 25 patients who received the therapy, with primary outcomes of CRS incidence by day 29 and secondary outcomes of mortality. All treated patients survived, 5 ventilated patients were extubated, and significant clinical improvements were seen within 72 hours, though pulmonary and systemic complications occurred in every case. The study’s single‐center, small‐sample design limits generalizability and highlights the need for larger, controlled trials to confirm efficacy and safety while monitoring for adverse events.

papers.title_zh: Efficacy and Safety of Sequential Combined Immunomodulatory Systemic Therapies Used in the Management of Refractory Cytokine Release Syndrome in Critically Ill Patients with COVID-19.
papers.source_body_en: Introduction/objective Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is characterized by systemic hyperinflammation and cytokine storm, a series of clinical conditions caused by excessive immune reactions. Although numerous studies have been conducted on anti-inflammatory treatments for severe COVID-19, no specific recommendations have been made regarding drugs to use in patients with Refractory Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) after the use of first-line anticytokine drugs. The objective of this report was to evaluate the efficacy of sequential immunomodulatory therapies in the management of refractory CRS in COVID-19 patients. Methods From March 2020 to March 2023, 1,025 patients with COVID-19 were admitted to the Infectious and Tropical Diseases ward at the Annunziata Cosenza Hub Hospital in Cosenza, Italy. To determine how many patients with refractory COVID-19-associated CRS were treated with combinedsequential therapy involving tocilizumab, a recombinant humanized anti-Interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor monoclonal antibody, and baricitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor, or anakinra, a recombinant human interleukin- 1 receptor antagonist, the electronic medical records of all hospitalized patients with COVID-19 were reviewed. The primary outcome was the incidence of CRS by day 29. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and 30-day mortality, to assess hospital performance and patient safety. Electronic databases such as MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Central were searched through June 30, 2026, for case-series and studies evaluating the efficacy of sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies in the management of refractory CRS in critically ill patients with COVID-19. Results From January 2021 to December 2023, a total of 25 patients received sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies, including tocilizumab and baricitinib or anakinra, in the management of COVID-19-related CRS. After 72 hours from the introduction of the new anti-cytokine therapy, a significant improvement of respiratory parameters, clinical state, inflammatory markers, and blood counts was observed. All patients survived, and those 5 previously mechanically ventilated patients were extubated. Non-infectious or infectious pulmonary or systemic complications were observed in all patients who underwent sequential combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies. Discussion The study's findings suggest that tocilizumab used in sequential combination with baricitinib or anakinra, in conjunction with standard of care treatments, was associated with improved outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19 disease and early discharge from the hospital. Conclusion There is clear rationale for using combined immunomodulatory systemic therapies in critically ill patients who develop refractory CRS. The results of the experience, supported by a review of the current literature, suggest the need for larger-scale studies on sequential and combined systemic immunomodulatory therapies to manage refractory CRS in critically ill patients with COVID-19.

papers.title: Does the messenger make the difference? Perceived reliability of health information sources during the COVID-19 pandemic in multi-ethnic Malaysia.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 infodemic highlighted the need to identify the extent to which health information messengers were perceived as reliable by the public in supporting effective public health communication. A question that remains is whether there are differences across ethnic groups in information processing. This study examines the perceived reliability of three formal sources (healthcare workers, scientists, and non-governmental organisations [NGOs]) and four informal sources (religious leaders, community leaders, interpersonal sources, and influencers) among Malaysia's multi-ethnic population through a cross-sectional online survey conducted between April and June 2021. Logistic regression was used to identify the perceived reliability of different information sources in steering vaccination intentions. We further examine the extent to which there were ethnic differences in the perceived reliability of these sources across education levels and age groups. Adjusted predicted probabilities were estimated to illustrate these differences. Among 5,784 participants, formal sources were consistently perceived as the most reliable across all ethnic groups and, together with community leaders, were identified as the main information sources influencing vaccination intention. We find large predicted probabilities of perceiving healthcare workers and scientists as reliable across most groups (≥ 80%), except among Indigenous groups who exhibit lower education attainment and are older (≤ 78%). Across education levels and age groups, Indians and Chinese exhibit higher predicted probabilities of perceiving NGOs as reliable, averaging approximately 80% and 75%, respectively, compared with approximately 65-70% among Malays and Indigenous groups. In contrast, predicted probabilities of perceiving community leaders as reliable were moderate across all ethnicities at the lowest education level and youngest age group (45 - 55%). This pattern remained relatively stable across higher education levels and age groups among Malays and Indigenous groups, but generally decreased among Chinese and Indian respondents. These results suggest that healthcare workers and scientists ought to remain central to health communication strategies, while NGOs and community leaders may play complementary roles. Multi-messenger approaches may enhance the effectiveness of public health responses during health crises.

papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate whether residency program unionization was associated with differences in resident well-being, learning environment, and mistreatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. BACKGROUND Resident unionization increased following the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by concerns regarding well-being and working conditions. However, evidence regarding the impact of unionization on resident outcomes remains limited. METHODS This difference-in-differences (DiD) study used data from a national survey administered to general surgery residents following the American Board of Surgery In-Training Examination from 2020 to 2023. We compared responses obtained before the pandemic (January 2020) and during the pandemic (January 2021), with 2022-2023 data included in sensitivity analyses. Residents from 310 programs (94.5% of eligible programs) were included, of which 30 (9.7%) were unionized. Outcomes included resident well-being (burnout, thoughts of attrition, and suicidal ideation), learning environment (duty-hour violations, protected educational time, and program responsiveness to resident concerns), and mistreatment. RESULTS A total of 13,539 responses were analyzed (response rates: 85.5% in 2020 and 81.2% in 2021). Unionization was not significantly associated with changes in burnout (DiD P=0.06), thoughts of attrition (DiD P=0.83), or suicidal ideation (DiD P=0.25). No significant differences were observed in duty-hour violations (DiD P=0.56) or protected educational time (DiD P=0.51). By 2023, nonunionized programs showed greater improvement in duty-hour violations (DiD P=0.003) and protected educational time (DiD P<0.001). Unionized programs demonstrated a transient improvement in program responsiveness to resident concerns during the initial pandemic period (DiD P=0.04), which did not persist by 2023 (DiD P=0.53). No differences were observed for mistreatment measures. CONCLUSIONS Unionization was not associated with improvements in resident well-being, the learning environment, or mistreatment during the pandemic, with the exception of a transient improvement in program responsiveness to resident concerns. These findings suggest that unionization alone may not be sufficient to protect resident wellness during periods of systemic stress.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: The review aims to evaluate whether residency program unionization was associated with differences in resident well-being, learning environment, and mistreatment during the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本差异-in-差异(DiD)研究使用了2020年至2023年间在全国范围内对普通外科住院医师进行的调查数据,这些数据是在美国外科委员会住院医师考试之后收集的。研究比较了大流行前(2020年1月)和大流行期间(2021年1月)的调查结果,并将2022-2023年的数据纳入敏感性分析。纳入了来自310个项目的住院医师(占所有符合条件项目的94.5%),其中30个(9.7%)为联合体项目。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在大流行期间,联合体与倦怠、离职念头或自杀念头的变化无显著关联。在值班时间违规或受保护的教育时间方面也未观察到显著差异。到2023年,非联合体项目在值班时间违规和受保护的教育时间方面显示出更大的改善。联合体项目在大流行初期显示出对住院医师关切的响应的短暂改善,但到2023年时这种改善不再持续。在不当对待指标方面未观察到差异。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些发现表明,仅靠联合体可能不足以在系统性压力时期保护住院医师的福祉。关于联合体对住院医师结果影响的证据仍然有限,且本研究未在大多数结果中发现显著差异,这表明在改善住院医师福祉和学习环境方面,联合体的作用仍存在理解上的空白。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本研究强调需要进一步研究以探讨联合体在改善住院医师福祉、学习环境和不当对待方面的有效性,特别是在像大流行这样的系统性压力背景下。

papers.title: Long-term prognostic value and clinical correlates of brain [18F]-FDG PET in patients with post-COVID-19 condition and neurocognitive disorders: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose : Brain [18F]-FDG-PET often reveals cerebral hypometabolism in post-COVID-19 patients experiencing neurocognitive issues, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. We evaluated the long-term utility of [18F]-FDG PET in this population. Materials and Methods: We reviewed the prospective SYNPOCov cohort (NCT05610436), including WHO-defined post-COVID-19 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 who underwent brain PET scans and had ≥1 year of follow-up. Final clinical outcomes were adjudicated as good (no residual disability), partial (improvement but persistent disability), or stable by an expert adjudication committee. PET scans were compared with those of age- and sex-matched pre-pandemic healthy controls (n=39). Regional metabolic values were extracted from significant clusters (voxel-level p Results: Seventy patients were included (48.3±11.9 years; 69% female; 26.4 ± 9.5 months follow-up), of whom 19, 34, and 17 were classified as having good, partial, and stable clinical outcomes respectively. Baseline imaging demonstrated hypometabolism in four clusters: right frontal, parietal and lateral temporal cortex, and cerebellum. Metabolic values in the right frontal and lateral temporal clusters were significantly lower in previously hospitalized patients and with pre-Omicron variants (p=≤0.04 and p=≤0.03 respectively). However, neither baseline regional metabolism nor its longitudinal evolution on follow-up PET scans (n=30) was associated with long-term clinical outcome. Conclusion: Brain [18F]-FDG PET remains a valuable biomarker of cerebral involvement in post-COVID-19 neurocognitive disorder, revealing metabolic signatures associated with acute disease severity and viral variant. While not predictive of long-term outcome, PET findings improve understanding of factors underlying persistent cerebral dysfunction. Trial registration number and date of registration: NCT05610436; 2022-01-07

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates the long-term prognostic value and clinical correlates of brain [18F]-FDG PET in patients with post-COVID-19 condition and neurocognitive disorders. The central question is whether baseline and longitudinal brain metabolic patterns can predict clinical outcomes in these patients.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a prospective cohort study based on the SYNPOCov cohort (NCT05610436), which includes WHO-defined post-COVID-19 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection who underwent brain PET scans and had ≥1 year of follow-up. The study compares PET scans with those of age- and sex-matched pre-pandemic healthy controls (n=39).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Baseline imaging showed hypometabolism in four clusters: right frontal, parietal and lateral temporal cortex, and cerebellum. Metabolic values in the right frontal and lateral temporal clusters were significantly lower in previously hospitalized patients and those infected with pre-Omicron variants. However, neither baseline regional metabolism nor its longitudinal evolution on follow-up PET scans was associated with long-term clinical outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study found that brain [18F]-FDG PET is not predictive of long-term clinical outcomes in post-COVID-19 patients with neurocognitive disorders. The findings suggest that while PET scans provide insights into cerebral involvement and metabolic signatures linked to acute disease severity and viral variant, they do not offer prognostic utility for long-term outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study highlights the need for further research to explore the role of brain [18F]-FDG PET in understanding persistent cerebral dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients. It also suggests that future studies should focus on identifying other biomarkers or factors that may better predict long-term outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study evaluates the long-term prognostic value of brain [18F]-FDG PET in post-COVID-19 patients with neurocognitive disorders. The study includes 70 patients with ≥1 year of follow-up and compares their PET scans with those of age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Baseline imaging revealed hypometabolism in four brain regions, with significant differences observed in previously hospitalized patients and those infected with pre-Omicron variants. However, neither baseline nor longitudinal metabolic patterns were associated with long-term clinical outcomes. The findings suggest that while PET scans provide insights into cerebral involvement and acute disease severity, they do not predict long-term prognosis. The study underscores the need for further research to identify more effective biomarkers for understanding persistent cerebral dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients.
